Three tins needed: a tail, a belly and a head.
A short rusty key. Fish slime still clings between the teeth.
A tail on the faded label. The fish inside has turned dark.
A belly on the worn label. The fish inside has darkened.
A head on the faded label. The fish lies in dark sludge.
The valve is chained shut. The padlock needs a key.
The key turns in the padlock.
There is no way through yet.
The door is locked. No one's lived here for a long time.
They took the chair apart and strapped it together. It can just about fit in the cabin like this.
Since the road collapsed, the cableway has been the only way out. They used to send whole loads of chairs out by truck.
The old people keep making chairs. Still waiting for the road to open.
They weighed visitors' luggage here. The needle is stuck, and no one needs it anymore.
Visitors used to put their suitcases here. The straps rotted with nothing on them.
They washed everything before leaving. No one left to sit here.

There are six chairs left in the house. Don't sell them one at a time. They were made for this table, although the table has already been taken away. A different table might be lower, and then the legs would need sawing down. Don't saw the legs: it's good old wood, and we won't find more like it.

We kept two chairs for visitors. They're covered with a sheet.

There won't be any more visitors, but leave the sheet on. Without it, they'll have to count as ordinary chairs, and we already have four of those. Four were enough when everyone lived here. Later, two were enough. Towards the end I sat on the one by the door: the others had already been washed before we left.

Don't prop the door open with anything.

I used the lowest chair, and now it always counts as occupied. While packing I tried to sit on it a few times. Sat on another one and washed it again.

If they open the house before we return, take the sheet off first. If not, leave everything as it is. Don't put the chairs outside: the ones that were supposed to leave before us are already out there. There's no room for these.
Elna is bending another chair back. The earlier chairs are still here, unsold.
Severin replaced the belt. The lathe hasn't earned anything in years.
They still cut new chair backs from the old templates. There's no one left to teach.
The seat is nearly woven. They're clearing more space for the finished chairs.
Made a walking frame out of chair parts. Something for their own use now.
A folding bed for guests. In the ski season, the houses couldn't hold everyone.
Families rented rooms to skiers. Chairs weren't their only income — every winter, they waited for visitors.
The rooms stayed empty after the avalanche. Now the guests and the owners are gone.
The Klaven children grew up and left. The bicycle stayed on its hooks.
A ladder from the guest bunks. They took the beds and left this.
The stone is still usable. They bring tools here less and less often.
The pattern in the iron is still intact. People used to queue here in the ski season.
This is where they promised to reopen the road. Then they stopped calling meetings.
They gave up waiting for the repairs and left. The application is still here.

Don't come to me about the road anymore. The copies are between the doors. The bottom one isn't signed: it mustn't be signed yet. They said the earlier work has to be approved first. It can't be approved because the road isn't finished. Finishing it requires a permit for new work. New work can't begin until the earlier work is approved.

I copied this without shortening it. Last time they said I hadn't followed the procedure. Now the whole procedure is here.

The office asked for someone to stay home for an inspection. They can't drive here: the vehicle can't get through. They won't come through the station because the equipment is assigned to the vehicle. I offered to meet them with a sled, but then the equipment would arrive separately from the inspection. That happened before, and now that inspection needs approving too.

If anyone does come, have them look at the support first. It started sinking back when we were waiting for the first permit. I won't prop it up anymore. I need the boards for the shutters. I'm closing the house, but I won't withdraw the application. They say that would mean starting again.
Skiers used to line up at this turnstile every winter. These slopes were what they came for.
The resort brought good money into the village. Now the turnstile is pushed against the wall — no one needs to pass through.
A pipe for every boot. All of them cold now.
You could still straighten a pair of skis. Nowhere to use them here.
Patches all over the canvas. The stretcher was still usable when the rescue service closed.
This bar was torn from the ski lift. The avalanche came down from the ridge.
It went through the forest and broke the upper support. The cable is still under the snow.
Fallen trees mixed in with the metal. It all weathered dark long ago; only the snow is fresh.
A vent hood from a service building. The avalanche crushed it along with the roof.
The main lodge survived. They never rebuilt the lift or the buildings around it.
You can shelter in the hall and light the stove. That isn't enough to keep a resort going.
The markings are still visible. No one straightened the gauge after the avalanche.
The seat was cut from a chair back. No one left here to ride it.
They checked the chairs for wobble here. Then the finished ones sat unused for years.
They hauled chairs to the big city in this. Just the body left, stripped of everything useful.
E — inspect the pile of chairs
The bottom seats have rotted. This load never left.
They still make new ones. There's room for them under a roof, for now.
Enough strapping left for plenty more loads. The rusty end has already snapped off.
When the avalanche wrecked the resort, a landslide took out part of the only road. They brought this winch up for the repairs.
That road brought tourists in and carried chairs out to the big city. There was no other way through for trucks.
They've been promising to restore the road for years. The politicians are still arguing, and the cable has seized on the drum.
The mix set inside the drum. The workers never came back.
The grease dried out under the cover. They never lifted the beam.
Drivers looked here for traffic coming from the big city. Now the road ends around the bend.
You can see the same towers from the checkpoint in our city. The big city is still over there, beyond the collapsed road.
They all squeezed into the shot. The man in the middle raised his bottle above their heads.
Skiers and locals outside the intact lodge. The picture sits in a worn wooden frame.
In the picture, the cable still runs over intact towers. The paper has yellowed at the edges.
The pole straps have gone stiff. Dust lies inside the boots.
A dry log with dark bark.
Crowbar — on the right belt loop

A steel crowbar with a bent end.
The paint has worn off the steel edges. The grip is rough.
Two barrels side by side. The wooden stock is worn.
Eight rounds in the magazine. The steel edges are worn.
Four rounds for the double barrel. The brass bases have darkened.

The receiver is cold. No dial tone.
Just damp cardboard and the smell.
The door is locked. The handle does not give.
I won't get there on foot.
I can't remember where the key to this door is.
A cheap bottle, almost empty. It smells sharply even through the cap.
One speckled egg in a battered carton. It might still be edible.
An opened can of stew. Cold fat has set around the meat.
You look hungry… If only I had something to feed you.
E — order the same drink again
The cashier stares at you in silence. He does not seem to blink.
Oh, a live one. Rare around here.
Off the grass. People are resting under it.
Shopping for a plot? Got one with a gate view.
Too early for you. Though, hard to say.
No guided tours. All the exhibits are lying down.
Walk around, walk around. Nobody here ever complained.
Bringing flowers is fine. Taking them out is bad luck.
What are you staring at? I'm the only temporary one here.
If you get lost, shout. We'll have a laugh together.
Looking for relatives, or just pricing things up?
They walk and they walk... and nobody wants to lie down.
Don't linger after sunset. Not because of the dead — because of me.
Leave the enclosure alone. It will outlive you.
Free entry for the living. For now.
I will get there. It is close.
The right hand will not obey.
The keys are in my pocket. I checked.
I need to sit. Not for long.
My head is heavy. It will pass.
I will sleep sitting up. Simpler.
Go home. If you remember where that is.
The wall is holding you. Thank it.
You can be smelled three houses off.
The pavement is not yours. Nor the legs.
Hold on to the air. It is steadier than you.
In front of everyone. Find a corner at least.
You are not walking. You are falling slowly.
Your kind ends up lying by the bus stop.
Disgusting to look at. And not to look at.
You sway, and I am the one feeling sick.
Make it to the corner: quite the feat.
Do not breathe this way. Breathe over there.
You are wider than the pavement. Stand straight.
One more like that and it is all fours.
Lean on something. The post will not mind.
You will not know yourself by morning. Good.
Legs apart, eyes apart. All of you apart.
Wish I had not seen this. No way round it.
Wherever it carries you, go there. Not here.
Walk on. The asphalt will not get softer.

The foam falls at once.
The bitterness lingers.

Sickly sweet.
It leaves a sour taste.

It smells of alcohol.
The first sip burns.

It reeks of alcohol.
It burns the throat.

A soft woven scarf. Covers the neck and lower half of the face.
That item is no longer there.
That would change nothing right now.
The item could not be consumed.
A worn ring with two keys. One is slightly bent.
A cheap metal lighter. It smells faintly of tobacco.
Half a litre of cheap vodka under a screw cap.
One small egg, sold individually without ceremony.
An opened can of stew. Cold fat has set around the meat.
A sealed tin that promises there might be meat inside.
A dry brick in a thin packet. The seasoning seems to be there.
Half a stale white loaf held by a grey paper band.
This package has no price tag.
This item is not for sale.
That spot on the shelf is already empty.
There is nowhere left to put it.
The cat on the stairwell landing is hungry. I should feed it a can of stew.
The cat has been fed. Now I can get on with my day.
I have to feed the cat first.
I'm not hungry yet. This one is for the cat.
There is one street and it goes up. The house stands at the top of it.
The house is open. Mother sits in her chair.
Mother is asking for a scarf. It is in the chest upstairs, in the parents' bedroom.
There is a scarf upstairs, in the chest. Put it on.
Have you eaten? There should be something in the stove.
Your father will come for supper.
Are you staying long? The bed upstairs is made.
Is the city still the same?
There is bread on the table. I cut it this morning.
The north window will not shut. It draughts.
The snow has not let up since morning.
The neighbours were asking about you.
The scarf is in the chest upstairs. Put it on.
It was biting this morning. Not now.
Wind's changed. That's it till evening.
Water's warm. So they're sitting deep.
Counting the catch before you're done is bad.
There'll be no rain. I watched the clouds.
No boats for hire. Ten years now.
It's deep here. Three metres, by the boards.
There used to be flounder. Now, I don't know.
I always let the first one go. That's how it's done.
The lamp doesn't help. Fish see light.
Home soon. I'll sit a while longer.
Not like this. I will wait.
The route was cancelled. I wait anyway.
There is petrol. There is no reason.
Twenty years on this run. Always the same place.
One headlight is gone. It still drives.
The last route has already gone. Or it has not yet.
The timetable is on the board. It lies.
I flip a coin. The answer never changes.
I am waiting. Not for you.
You have not got it on you. I would have noticed.
Nobody gets driven back this way.
Twenty years up here. First time not alone.
Engine cools down, and that's that.
I'll wait. I'm used to it.
Still got the coin. Nowhere to toss it.
You got here. That's rare enough.
Wind blows here dawn to dawn.
If you're smoking, go round the far side.
Take off your coat. Leave the rest to me.
Take another drag. I like watching.
Sit closer. We won't need the coffee.
I remember: you teased me all evening.
One more minute and I stop holding back.
You decided to provoke me again.
Decency ends at the door with you.
The bed squeaked till dawn. Wasn't me.
Take it off yourself. Don't be slow.
Then watch. Keep your hands to yourself.
Wait. I'll make the first move.
The bed is far. I won't wait that long.
Finish the coffee. You'll need strength.
You gave in too quickly that night.
Don't wait. I'm tired of holding back too.
About time. Don't be shy with me.
Yes. You were tired long before dawn.
Take your coat. It's warmer at home.
I'm not asleep. I'm waiting for you.
It's time to go home. I'm here.
In draughts they think with the knee.
A draught goes forward. Back would shame it.
That is no game. You shuffle bottle caps.
Draughts is chess with the thought taken out.
A king there is a pawn promoted for service.
Your whole thought fits on one diagonal.
Thirty-two squares, and all of them missed.
Takes three in a row and glows like a stove.
Your king is two draughts stacked up.
No mate in draughts. So nothing to discuss.
A game for men who cannot tell pieces apart.
You are not playing. You are sweeping.
The knight moves like a letter. A sad one.
Two hours of thinking to lose in a minute.
A bishop on one colour for life. Like you.
Castling is a king running round a corner.
Sixteen pieces and not one idea in them.
You have no game. You have social classes.
The queen works, the rest stand. Familiar?
You do not play. You recite other men.
En passant. The name alone says enough.
Chess was invented to keep silent nicely.
Your game ends in a draw. Like the rest.
More rules than players at this table.
At last. Sit, do not hover.
I have White. Do not dawdle.
A piece was there. Now it is not.
Thank you. I will take that.
So the fourth stool was good for something.
Eaten. And I will eat again.
Do not offer them. I will take.
The pawn got there. A queen now.
A queen. Out of a pawn, mind.
Not that one. There is a take.
“A grave wants digging. You up for it?”   E — I am,   Q — not today
The plot is marked out. Find your own spade.
Suit yourself. The work will keep.
The hole is ready. The coffin next.
Down it goes. Now fill it in.
The earth is back. The stone now.
Done. Straighter than the last man’s. Now back to the watchman for the money.

Haven't seen you in a while.
Just stepped out for a minute.
The watchman marked out a vacant plot at the cemetery. Dig the hole, lower the coffin, fill it in and set the stone.
The grave is closed and the stone is up. The watchman settles up at his window.
Thanks. We can get through now.
Don't mind the old car. The engine's still good.
I know every pothole here. Still hit one now and then.
They patch this road every year. It never lasts long.
Just had the suspension done. Something's knocking again already.
Petrol's gone up again. Feels like I'm always filling up.
I used to drive nights as well. These days I try to finish early.
Don't worry, we'll get there fine. I've been driving here for twenty years.
You sit down all day, and your back still aches by evening.
Even the car's quieter on a good road.
It's not far. Just nowhere to pick up speed.
Don't rummage in there. That's my loose change.
What is this shit we're listening to? The composer is utterly talentless
My sleeve keeps catching on the fence.
Roll it up. Mine did that too.
They will soften by the radiator.
The wind gets under my collar.
The seam digs in the other way.
It is wet over the side too.
We can hear your crane from out at sea.
That winch has hummed for ages.
Does that trolley wheel still rattle?
It does. The store is close enough.
The wind shifts it a little.
Were you rolling much at the entrance?
It settled down by the pier.
Hello. Is that a new jacket?
Patched the old one. Still good.
Welcome back. How is it aboard?
Wet boots. Everything else is fine.
Got home yesterday and fell asleep.
I managed to heat up dinner first.
The sea seems quieter from shore.
You cannot hear it by the crane.
No more crates until tonight, I hope.
No more crates at all would suit me.
My back just starts aching earlier.
My wife put the bottle behind the cupboard.
My wife wants to go dancing.
I can barely get my boots off after work.
She is saving for a coat again.
Do not ask how much she still needs.
Did you buy her those flowers?
I did. All the leaves fell off on the way.
Three days fixing a stool at home.
My door has squeaked for six months.
I would like one trip out to sea.
Get some boots without holes first.
Sick of pulling this lever all day.
I still hear that hum at home.
I said I would do nothing on my day off.
They will still send you out for bread.
The mugs at the bar are small again.
Plenty of foam over the rim, though.
Short waves past the pier today.
I will watch them from shore.
At least you get a different shore.
I cannot see it from the hold.
We will get beer when you come ashore.
I still have the deck to scrub.
My girlfriend changed her haircut again.
Mine has started cutting hers short too.
Was it rolling much out there?
Sloshed the tea out of my mug.
I could use something strong after this trip.
They want a shelf put up at home.
Mine has been by the wall for three weeks.
Will you get home today, captain?
Promised to be back for dinner. They will wait again.
See you. Keep warm over there.
Take care, lads. Dry those boots.
We will. You keep dry too.
Bye. Do not stay here all night.
See you. Zip up your jacket.
Done. Do not lose your gloves.
Bye. We will finish talking next time.
All right. You know where to find me.
The cab smells of fish again.
My coat smells like that all winter.
Still need to stop for bread.
My wife told me to scrub the seats.
Mine won't let these gloves in the house.
Get any sleep on your day off?
The neighbour was drilling all morning.
My lunch went cold in the cab again.
My tea's been cold since morning.
See you. Do your coat up.
The puddle by the stop is ankle-deep again.
That's twice I've soaked my socks there.
Went to get bread. The price is up again.
And the loaf keeps getting smaller.
The radiator at home is barely warm.
I get a draught by the window all evening.
My jacket still hasn't dried since this morning.
Hang it away from the door.
These cobbles wear my boots out every month.
I've got another nail poking out of my heel.
Tried going for a walk on my day off. Got chilled again.
I only went to the shop and back.
The neighbour's pipe hummed all night.
I get enough of that noise during the day.
The wind goes straight through my collar.
My sleeves have been damp for two days.
They want more for the room again.
They could at least fix the window for that money.
These stairs leave my knees aching by evening.
I stop on every landing with my shopping bag.
Got both sleeves wet on the walk to the port.
An umbrella just turns inside out here.
There's a draught by the door at the bar.
Sit further in. I got a chill in my back there.
They promised a dry day. My sleeves are wet again.
My gloves have been damp since morning.
A room in town costs half your wages now.
Can't get out of the wind on shore either.
Haven't dried my jacket since the last trip.
No use hanging it by the door at home.
Walked all over town. No boots in my size.
I sent mine in for repairs again.
My fingers froze waiting for the bus.
I walk now. At least you keep moving.
The road is full of holes. Spilled my whole lunch.
I picked up all the mud on my boots there.
Hope the wind drops by evening.
I just want my wipers to stop squeaking.
Everything in the shop costs more again.
I put half of it back on the shelf yesterday.
Can't feel my fingers when the wind comes off the sea.
It's not warm down in my hold either.
The ceiling at home dripped all night.
We still have a bucket by the window.
Shift over, and another walk home in a damp jacket.
I put a rag over my seat.
Greased it this morning. It's the pulley.
Can't get any peace with this wind.
Going to push that trolley till tomorrow?
Have to tell you everything twice.
Nothing but crates, and my back already aches.
Just sat down, and there's clattering everywhere.
My tea's gone cold again because of you lot.
The handle needs another push again.
Those lids keep ringing in my ears.
I can still hear them at home.
My back won't straighten till evening.
Bent over already. Half a shift left.
There's a draught from the door.
Mine too. Right at the toe.
There's a thread on your sleeve.
I keep meaning to cut it off.
I'll get some bread after the shift.
I can stand a while longer.
Sand's crunching under the wheels again.
We'll be sweeping it out till evening.
You can feel the cold from those crates.
I could hear the truck from inside.
The sleeve wears out faster here.
Mine's worn through at the elbow.
The cans are running smoother today.
The wind doesn't get down my collar here.
You've been saying that for a while.
The wood runs out by morning.
We will break up another crate.
The smoke keeps coming my way.
Sit over here, I am not holding the spot.
The wind is meaner under the arch than out there.
Move the bottles, you will step on one.
I will pick them up in the morning.
The cardboard is damp, it will not catch.
What time is it by now?
The lamps are on. Still night.
My back will stiffen by morning.
Turn your back to the fire.
You can light one off the barrel.
The barrel has burnt through at the bottom.
It will be back by morning.
He is snoring for the whole corner again.
Let him. At least one of us sleeps.
Rub them. Keep them out of the fire.
It was cleaner here last week.
My boot is coming apart at the toe.
I could use some hot tea.
There is boiling water. No tea.
The frost will bite by morning.
The mattress is damp on your side.
I will turn it over in the day.
Mind you do not fall asleep by them.
You are snoring for the whole arch.
Move over, your feet are in the fire.
I am warm as it is.
I will wake you in the morning.
All right. I'll bring it over.
All right. I'll get it ready.
All right. I'll bring it here.
We have that one. I'll bring it.
All right. I'll put it in front of you.
I'll be right over. I'll pour it.
Same again. I'll pour it now.
All right. I remember the drink.
All right. I'll bring another of the same.
We still have that drink. I'll pour it.
I'll bring another of the same now.
The beer's flat. Still bitter, though.
The foam's still holding. It won't last.
The head looks decent. It'll settle soon.
The head went down while I carried it.
The tap won't fix the taste.
This beer doesn't fizz for long.
The mug's clean. It's the beer that's bitter.
Looks better in the mug than it tastes.
There's only one beer. Not much to choose from.
Handle on the right. The foam won't last.
They don't skimp on sugar. You can taste it.
This wine's too sweet even for me.
Cheap wine. The glass is better.
Looks like wine. Tastes too sweet.
The sugar hasn't covered the sour taste.
Not much to say about this wine.
Fortified, like the menu says. Sour as usual, too.
The glass is fine. The wine isn't much.
You still get the sour taste under the sugar.
Unaged. You can smell it straight away.
Harsh. The glass doesn't change that.
Smells of alcohol. Nothing covering it.
The glass is too fancy for this.
They call it a distillate. Alcohol is what you smell first.
Burns straight away. No surprises there.
You can smell it while it's pouring.
Sharp smell. That's how it comes.
Smells of alcohol. Never noticed anything else.
Small shot glass. Burns as usual.
You can tell by the smell without the label.
It's nicer with the bottle closed.
I don't promise much with this vodka.
Clear. Nothing smooth about the taste.
The shot glass is clean. Same vodka as ever.
Bread's gone up a little again.
I buy half a loaf now. Lasts until tomorrow.
Nothing but small coins in my pocket.
Just right for the bus. Keep them.
The sole's coming away at the edge.
The repair shop still takes those. They glued mine back.
The light on our stairs barely works.
Someone should wipe the shade first. It's all grey.
The bus stood by the turn for ages today.
They were unloading there. One lane isn't enough.
I need to collect a parcel in the morning.
Go when they open. There's a queue later.
My fingers still smell of paint.
Mine did after the railings. Went away in a couple of days.
My key keeps catching on the lining.
Put it in another pocket. Sew this one later.
I'm wearing two pairs of socks at home now.
I've got a mat under my feet. The floor's cold.
They're moving the lockers at work again.
As long as they don't change the keys. Mine at least locks.
The potatoes at the bottom of the sack are all soft.
I take them from the crate now. You can see each one.
They painted the bench by the entrance.
The old coat's still peeling off the back.
My collar rubs my neck by evening.
I've got the same seam. Goes rough after washing.
About twenty minutes on foot. Nearly as long by bus.
The shop had no change again.
They asked me for coins at the till. Everyone brings big notes.
The radiator's cold on one side.
They flushed ours out first. Heated evenly after that.
I keep meaning to move the alarm clock.
Put it further from the bed. Helps me.
My old one did too. Had to tighten the buckle.
Today's lunch is still in my bag.
Warm it up at home. I'm carrying mine back too.
The neighbour keeps slamming the door.
Their closer doesn't hold. You hear it all morning.
They charge for bags at the market now.
I keep one in my bag. Still in one piece.
How much did the sole cost you?
Nearly half a new boot. At least it's dry now.
I've got one like that. No use on tight screws.
The rain eased off at lunch yesterday.
I carry my jacket anyway. Still have to walk back.
The washing's on its second day drying.
Move the rack away from the wall. That corner's damp at mine.
The old zip didn't split. I keep fixing this one.
Last time it took until evening. Bring your lunch.
The kiosk serves coffee in a smaller cup now.
Same lid. Just a shorter cup.
Hold it at the bottom. Mine still does up that way.
They've dug up the path by my building again.
I go round through the yard. Saves my shoes, at least.
I go in the mornings now. Evenings are booked up.
The rice from lunch stuck to the pan.
I leave the lid a little open. Burns less often.
They put a new clock up in the shop.
The people at the tills still check their own.
Don't pinch the seal. Ours did that after they changed it.
My shoulder aches from the bag.
Mine has the same narrow strap. I carry it by hand on the way home.
They want another group photo at work.
They could give me a uniform first. The old one's stained.
Day after tomorrow. Still have to go to the office in the morning.
I keep thinking of taking the shelving apart.
Label the boxes first. You won't find anything afterwards.
I'll only sit here a little while today.
Same here. Washing to take down at home.
Try them with the boot on. Mine are too thick.
I decide that every evening. Still rush in the morning.
A packet of nails spilled all through my bag.
